chunks: And Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Uqda al-Kufi informed us, saying: Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Shayban narrated to me from his book in the year 273 AH, saying: Ali ibn Sayf ibn Umayra narrated to me, saying: Abban ibn Uthman narrated from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (as) from his fathers (as) that:

The Prophet (S) said: 'Among my Ahl al-Bayt there are twelve inspired men (Muhaddathun).' A man called Abdullah ibn Zayd, who was the foster-brother of Ali ibn al-Husayn (as), said to him: 'Glory be to Allah! Inspired?' as if he were denying it. Imam Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (as) turned to him and said: 'By Allah, the son of your mother (Ali ibn al-Husayn) was indeed inspired.'

key_terms.عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ زَيْدٍ: Abdullah ibn Zayd (the narrator asking the question)
key_terms.عَلِيٌّ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ: Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin, the fourth Imam)
key_terms.مُحَدَّثًا: Inspired man (one who receives divine inspiration)

ai.seo_question: Who are the twelve inspired men from the Prophet's family according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* establishes the twelve Imams as *Muhaddathun* (inspired ones), a status distinct from prophethood but indicative of divine communication. The specific mention of Ali ibn al-Husayn (as) serves to validate the lineage and spiritual authority of the Ahl al-Bayt, countering early skeptics who questioned whether non-prophets could receive such inspiration. This hadith is foundational in Shia theology for defining the Imams' role as inheritors of the Prophet's knowledge and divine guidance.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (6) Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sa’eed bin Oqda al-Kufi narrated from Yahya bin Zakariyya bin Shayban from Ali bin Sayf bin Omayra from Abban bin Uthman from Zurara from Imam Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as) from his fathers (as) that the Prophet (S) had said: “From among my progeny there will be twelve inspired men.”

A man called Abdullah bin Zayd, who was the foster-brother of Ali bin al-Husayn as-Sajjad (as), said to him (to Imam al-Baqir): “Glory be to Allah! Inspired!” as if he denied that. Imam Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as) said to him: “By Allah, the son of your mother -he meant Ali bin al-Husayn (as)- was indeed inspired.”
